claims.text: GDACS's tropical cyclone report for DUJUAN-26 (event id 1001322) tracked the storm over the Northwest Pacific from 15 to 22 September 2026 with maximum sustained winds of 130 km/h, assessing an Overall Green alert for Japan (GDACS score 0.5) under its automated wind-exposure model, which estimates no population within Category 1 or higher wind zones and does not capture the storm's rainfall-driven flood and landslide impact documented separately by Japanese authorities.

claims.source_name: Japan Fire and Disaster Management Agency (FDMA)
claims.text: Japan's Fire and Disaster Management Agency situation report No. 8 (22 September 2026, 12:30 JST) on Typhoon No. 25: 5 deaths (Chiba 3, Kanagawa 1, Miyazaki 1), 3 people missing, 20 injured, and 468 homes damaged (18 total collapse, 5 half collapse, 325 flooded above floor level, 54 flooded below floor level, 22 partially damaged). Evacuation instructions covered 36,711 households (74,289 people) across Chiba, Tokyo and Kanagawa. A Level 5 special warning for landslides was issued for Oshima Town, Tokyo, at 12:40 on 21 September and downgraded to Level 4 by 23:00 the same day; Chiba (12:30, 21 Sept), Tokyo (11:00, 21 Sept) and Kanagawa (16:30, 21 Sept) each established prefectural disaster response headquarters.

claims.source_name: Japan Fire and Disaster Management Agency (FDMA)
claims.text: Japan's Fire and Disaster Management Agency situation report No. 10 (23 September 2026, 12:00 JST) on Typhoon No. 25: 10 deaths (Chiba: Mobara 1, Kamogawa 2, Sodegaura 1, Inzai 1, Sanmu 1; Kanagawa: Yokosuka 2, Miura 1; Miyazaki: Nichinan 1), 4 people missing (2 from a Kamogawa landslide, 1 from a Yokosuka landslide, 1 from a Miura landslide), 42 injured, and 659 homes damaged or destroyed (22 total collapse, 10 half collapse, 410 flooded above floor level, 180 flooded below floor level, 37 partially damaged). Evacuation instructions had been reduced to 509 households (1,062 people): 464 households (996 people) in Chiba and 45 households (66 people) in Kanagawa.

claims.source_name: Japan Fire and Disaster Management Agency (FDMA)
claims.text: Japan's Fire and Disaster Management Agency situation report No. 13 (24 September 2026, 17:00 JST) on Typhoon No. 25: 12 deaths (of which 3 disaster-related; Chiba: Mobara 1, Kamogawa 3, Sodegaura 1, Inzai 1, Sanmu 1; Kanagawa: Yokosuka 3, Miura 1; Miyazaki: Nichinan 1), 3 people missing (a Kamogawa landslide, a Nagara-machi landslide and a Miura landslide, each with one person unaccounted for), 28 injured (1 serious, 27 minor), and 828 homes damaged or destroyed (29 total collapse, 33 half collapse, 469 flooded above floor level, 255 flooded below floor level, 42 partially damaged). Evacuation instructions remained at 509 households (1,062 people): 464 households (996 people, 2 cities and 1 town) in Chiba and 45 households (66 people, 1 city) in Kanagawa. Tokyo's Oshima Town Level 5 landslide special warning, issued 21 September, had already been downgraded to Level 4 the same day, and Chiba, Tokyo and Kanagawa prefectures remain under their disaster response headquarters established 21 September.

description: Typhoon Dujuan, Japan's Typhoon No. 25, brought record rainfall and violent winds to eastern Japan from 20 to 23 September 2026, triggering floods and landslides across the Kanto region. Japan Meteorological Agency issued a Level 5 special warning for landslides on Tokyo's Izu Oshima island on 21 September, and Chiba, Tokyo and Kanagawa prefectures each stood up disaster response headquarters. Japan's Fire and Disaster Management Agency's latest situation report (24 September) records 12 deaths -- seven in Chiba, four in Kanagawa and one in Miyazaki -- plus 3 people still missing, 28 injured and 828 homes damaged or destroyed. Evacuation instructions, which peaked at more than 74,000 people across Chiba, Tokyo and Kanagawa on 21-22 September, have held steady at about 1,060 people as damage assessment continues.

impact.summary: Japan's Fire and Disaster Management Agency's situation report No. 13 (24 September 2026, 17:00 JST) records 12 deaths (3 disaster-related; Chiba 7, Kanagawa 4, Miyazaki 1), 3 people still missing from landslides in Kamogawa, Nagara-machi and Miura, 28 injured, and 828 homes damaged or destroyed (29 total collapse, 33 half collapse, 469 flooded above floor level, 255 flooded below floor level, 42 partially damaged). Evacuation instructions remain at about 1,062 people (509 households) in Chiba and Kanagawa, unchanged from the prior report, as damage assessments continue in flood- and landslide-affected areas.

name: Typhoon Dujuan (Typhoon No. 25), Japan

updates.text: FDMA's situation report No. 13 (24 September, 17:00 JST) raised the toll to 12 deaths (3 disaster-related; Chiba 7, Kanagawa 4, Miyazaki 1) and damaged homes to 828, while missing fell to 3 (Kamogawa, Nagara-machi and Miura landslides) and injured fell to 28. Evacuation instructions held steady at 509 households (1,062 people) in Chiba and Kanagawa.

FDMA's situation report No. 10 (23 September, 12:00 JST) raised the toll to 10 deaths (Chiba 6, Kanagawa 3, Miyazaki 1) and 42 injured, with 4 still missing from landslides in Kamogawa, Yokosuka and Miura; damaged homes rose to 659. Evacuation instructions were scaled back to about 1,062 people, down from a 21-22 September peak of 74,289.

FDMA's situation report No. 8 (22 September, 12:30 JST) recorded 5 deaths, 3 missing and 468 damaged homes; evacuation instructions covered 74,289 people across Chiba, Tokyo and Kanagawa. Tokyo's Oshima Town had been placed under a Level 5 landslide special warning on 21 September, downgraded to Level 4 by 23:00 the same day.
